hook.en: Every Shape has an area, but there is no formula for "a shape". Java lets you promise a method without writing it: abstract classes and interfaces.

objectives.en: Declare abstract classes and abstract methods
Choose between an abstract class and an interface

narration.en: Every Shape has an area, but there is no formula for "a shape". Java lets you promise a method without writing it: abstract classes and interfaces.

body.en: An abstract class is declared with abstract and cannot be instantiated (no new Shape()). It may contain abstract methods, declared without a body (abstract double area();), as well as ordinary fields, constructors and methods. A concrete subclass must override every abstract method, or itself be declared abstract. Abstract classes capture what related classes share while leaving the details to each subclass.

explanation.en: An abstract class is a partial class: it has state and constructors and is extended once. An interface holds constants and method promises and may be implemented many times.

body.en: An interface is a reference type containing constants and abstract methods (Java 8 also allows default and static methods with bodies). Its fields are automatically public static final, and its abstract methods public abstract. A class implements an interface with implements and must define all its abstract methods as public. A class may implement many interfaces, and an interface may extend other interfaces. A variable of an interface type can refer to any implementing object, which gives polymorphism.

passage.en: __1__ class Shape { abstract double area(); } class Circle __2__ Shape { double r; double area() { return Math.PI * r * r; } } interface Drawable { void draw(); } class Square extends Shape __3__ Drawable { double s; double area() { return s * s; } public void draw() { … } } A Shape variable may hold a Circle, but new Shape() is __4__.

explanation.en: Shape is abstract and extended; Drawable is an interface and implemented; abstract classes cannot be instantiated, which the compiler reports.
